entries.name: Erlang
entries.definition: A functional programming language, originally developed at Ericsson, designed for concurrent, fault-tolerant systems.

entries.name: Ewondo
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken by the Beti people of central Cameroon, around Yaoundé.

entries.name: F#
entries.definition: A functional-first programming language for the .NET platform, developed at Microsoft Research.

entries.name: F*
entries.definition: A proof-oriented, ML-family functional programming language for writing and verifying programs, developed by Microsoft Research and Inria.

entries.name: Fali
entries.definition: A group of related languages spoken by the Fali people of northern Cameroon.

entries.name: Fantom
entries.definition: A general-purpose, object-oriented programming language that targets the Java Virtual Machine, .NET and JavaScript.

entries.name: Filipino
entries.definition: The standardized form of Tagalog and the national language of the Philippines.

entries.name: Finnish
entries.definition: A Uralic language, the main language of Finland.

entries.name: Forth
entries.definition: A stack-based, extensible programming language created by Charles H. Moore.

entries.name: Fortran
entries.definition: One of the oldest high-level programming languages, created at IBM in the 1950s and still widely used for numerical and scientific computing.

entries.name: French
entries.definition: A Romance language spoken in France and many other countries.

entries.name: Frisian
entries.definition: A group of closely related West Germanic languages spoken in the Netherlands and Germany, of which West Frisian is the most widely spoken.

entries.name: Fula
entries.definition: A Niger-Congo language spoken by the Fulani people as a chain of dialects across West and Central Africa.

entries.name: Gaelic
entries.definition: The Goidelic Celtic languages, namely Irish, Scottish Gaelic and Manx, with the word most often meaning Scottish Gaelic or Irish depending on context.

entries.name: Galo
entries.definition: A Tibeto-Burman language spoken mainly in Arunachal Pradesh, India.

entries.name: Gambas
entries.definition: A free, object-oriented BASIC-like programming language and development environment for Linux.

entries.name: Garifuna
entries.definition: An Arawakan language spoken by the Garifuna people along the Caribbean coast of Central America.

entries.name: German
entries.definition: A West Germanic language spoken mainly in Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

entries.name: Gherkin
entries.definition: A plain-text domain-specific language that uses Given, When and Then keywords to write behaviour specifications that tools such as Cucumber can run.

entries.name: Gikuyu
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken mainly by the Kikuyu people of central Kenya.

entries.name: Go
entries.definition: A statically typed, compiled programming language designed at Google, known for simple syntax and built-in concurrency.

entries.name: GraphQL
entries.definition: A query language for APIs, with a server-side runtime, that lets clients ask for exactly the data they need.

entries.name: Greek
entries.definition: An Indo-European language forming its own Hellenic branch, spoken mainly in Greece and Cyprus.

entries.name: Groovy
entries.definition: A dynamic programming language for the Java Virtual Machine, with syntax close to Java's, used for scripting and build files.

entries.name: Gujarati
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken mainly in the Indian state of Gujarat.

entries.name: Hack
entries.definition: A programming language for the HipHop Virtual Machine, developed at Facebook as a statically typed dialect of PHP.

entries.name: Haitian Creole
entries.definition: A French-based creole language, one of the two official languages of Haiti.

entries.name: Hardware description language
entries.definition: A class of specialised computer languages, such as VHDL and Verilog, used to describe the structure and behaviour of electronic circuits.

entries.name: Haskell
entries.definition: A purely functional programming language with lazy evaluation and a strong static type system.

entries.name: Hausa
entries.definition: A Chadic language of the Afroasiatic family, spoken mainly in northern Nigeria and Niger and used as a lingua franca in West Africa.

entries.name: Havyaka Kannada
entries.definition: A dialect of Kannada traditionally spoken by the Havyaka Brahmin community in Karnataka and nearby areas.

entries.name: Hawaiian
entries.definition: A Polynesian language native to Hawaii and one of the two official languages of the state.

entries.name: Haxe
entries.definition: A high-level, cross-platform programming language and compiler that can produce code for targets such as JavaScript, C++ and the JVM.

entries.name: Haya
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken by the Haya people, mainly in the Kagera region of northwestern Tanzania.

entries.name: Hebrew
entries.definition: A Semitic language and the main official language of Israel.

entries.name: Hindi
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language written in the Devanagari script and an official language of India.

entries.name: Hmong
entries.definition: A group of related Hmong-Mien languages spoken by the Hmong people in China, Southeast Asia and diaspora communities.

entries.name: Hokkien
entries.definition: A group of Southern Min varieties of Chinese from Fujian, also spoken in Taiwan and Southeast Asia.

entries.name: Hopi
entries.definition: A Uto-Aztecan language spoken by the Hopi people of northeastern Arizona.

entries.name: HTML
entries.definition: Structuring web documents with HTML.
